focus: ClayEnv semantic identity and pre-ClayOS release trust admission
observed: Current public ClayOS launch is artifact-only and the current ClayEnv manifest binds source, grammar, executable IR, VM blob and artifact hashes.
The current ClayCode structured AST already carries Module.name, but ClayEnvManifest/v1 remains a single-source artifact manifest rather than a canonical module/package manifest.
A stale/diverged branch contained a useful external trusted-manifest-digest boundary but was not current-main integrated.
Parallel current research independently isolated the canonical module-resolution fusion gap; that remains compatible with this release-trust lane.

bounded_unusual_experiment.name: CLAYENV_PACKAGE_ROOT_RELOCATION
bounded_unusual_experiment.treatment: Identical Clay source bytes were placed under materially different directory roots and different source/artifact/manifest filenames.
bounded_unusual_experiment.required_result: Build result objects, artifact bytes and canonical manifest bytes remain identical, and both strict ClayOS launches return 42.
bounded_unusual_experiment.interpretation: No hidden host-root or filename coupling was detected in current ClayEnv build identity for identical Clay source bytes.
bounded_unusual_experiment.rollback: Test-only candidate; merged delta is one regression test and can be reverted independently.

mechanism: clayenv build reports the canonical manifest SHA-256 without changing ClayCode/TypedIR/VM semantics.
clayenv run requires trusted_manifest_sha256 as an input from outside the candidate artifact/manifest pair.
Manifest bytes must match that digest before canonical manifest parsing, artifact provenance checks and ClayOS.exec_artifact.
A different internally valid replacement manifest is rejected when presented under the original external manifest digest.
external_manifest_trust_boundary.claim_boundary: This is a trust-input interface, not an authenticated release-root authority.

grf_collapse.generated_reality: ClayEnv identity might accidentally depend on filesystem placement, making packages non-relocatable.
grf_collapse.counter_reality: Build identity is content/provenance based and relocation invariant.
grf_collapse.release_reality: An internally coherent artifact+manifest pair is sufficient release authority.
grf_collapse.release_counter_reality: A coherent pair still needs an independently anchored trust origin before execution.

architecture_delta.decision: Preserve path-independent ClayEnv build identity and require an external trusted-manifest digest before launch, while keeping actual release-root authentication outside the candidate bundle.
architecture_delta.parallel_frontier: Canonical module/use identity and module-resolution fusion remain OPEN and should converge with release-manifest construction rather than create a second parser or package semantics path.

remaining_falsifiers: Define ClayReleaseManifest/v1 around an independently provisioned/pinned release root using standards-aligned mechanisms rather than custom cryptography.
Add release epoch/rollback rejection and prove stale-but-valid metadata cannot re-admit an older artifact.
Define root rotation/recovery semantics and fail closed when no trusted root is available.
Fuse canonical module/package closure identity into release construction once lossless module/use semantics are available.
Re-run exact self-hosted Ubuntu admission after those bytes change.
non_claims: No caller-provided digest is treated as trust authority by itself.
No Linux interoperability authority was widened.
No second ClayVM or ClayOS execution path was added.
No whole Clay Machine acceptance is claimed.
No final/model training was authorized or started.
